title: Blackpoint details ROMULUS ClickFix chain delivering CNCMachineRMS remote access trojan
date_note: Date of Blackpoint Cyber report; Blackpoint says its tracking of high-volume ClickFix activity began in late September 2026.
place: No victim or region stated by the sources
summary: Blackpoint Cyber's report says ROMULUS, a ClickFix delivery platform, installs a remote access trojan it identified as CNCMachineRMS with high confidence. The trojan supports remote desktop control, screen streaming, microphone and camera capture and file management. Blackpoint says it observed no post-exploitation activity, assesses that ROMULUS likely operates as a delivery service, and names no victims or regions.
plain: Researchers describe a fake-verification trick that gets people to run a command, which installs a remote-control tool able to watch the screen, microphone and camera.
exec: A remote access trojan spread through user-run commands bypasses many controls; Blackpoint saw no follow-on activity yet.
action: Per Blackpoint: use application allowlisting, limit local admin rights, train users on ClickFix prompts, and hunt for PowerShell downloading installers, silent msiexec runs and DNS-over-HTTPS from unexpected processes.
impact: No victims, sectors or counts stated.

validation.note: Vendor original (Blackpoint Cyber, 18 Nov) read in full; primary source; The Hacker News (20 Nov) reports it and cites Forescout's earlier ROMULUS report.

review.note: Compared title, date, summary, capabilities, no post-exploitation, delivery-service wording and mitigations against Blackpoint and The Hacker News; match. Fixed date_note: late September is when Blackpoint's tracking of ClickFix activity began, not a stated ROMULUS start.
